parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no traveler-facing exposure: no facility bans, no police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, no trans-specific violence pattern, and no entry restrictions — border treatment is an open question, not an exposure. Documented positives: hate-crime law covering gender identity, a 2013 gender-marker recognition framework, and a 2026 legal-journal framework regulating how police, customs and court officers must search trans persons (suggesting state-aware treatment, albeit with 'search difficulties'). Countervailing signals are real but tier 3: inconsistent enforcement of anti-discrimination provisions, inadequate hate-crime investigation, under-reporting from fear of victimisation, escalating anti-gender disinformation including a parliamentary session, and a disrupted Pride. No documented remedy failure reaches visitors as direct exposure. This sits above anchors with traveller incidents and enforced friction, below anchors with strong working protections, in Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. Dossier states sources say nothing about visa rules, passport markers or entry procedures for trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Legal-journal analysis implies customs officers operate under a documented framework for searching trans/gender-nonconforming persons, though border practice is uncertain.
entry_documents.interaction: If a customs or police stop occurs, the search-of-trans framework governs conduct, but its practical quality ('search difficulties') is uncertain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented as traveller-facing; prison-sentences law treatment of trans persons is analysed in scholarship, no abusive custody practice shown.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented statutory framework for handling trans persons in criminal procedure and detention.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Framework exists but the record does not show how it operates in live custody; case studies of search difficulties suggest friction.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility or bathroom restrictions appear in the record.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination provisions nominally cover health, housing, education.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Equality bodies' monitoring shapes the domestic framework but visitors cannot invoke it directly.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors. IVF exclusion of same-sex couples is a resident-couple matter; blood-donation bar is sexuality-linked.
care_services.protection: Life Partnership Act Article 68 guarantees equal health-insurance and healthcare rights for life partners.
care_services.interaction: Documented enforcement gaps in health discrimination provisions may soften real-world recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented escalating anti-gender disinformation: 2024 parliamentary 'Gender Ideology' session with misinformation and no LGBTI participation; disrupted first Pride in a coastal city.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime legislation enumerates gender identity; open military service; formal LGR since 2013.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Political hostility is climate-level; no documented state action against trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling families. School-textbook homophobia was remedied by ministerial action in 2013.
minors_guardians.protection: Constitutional Court rulings protect same-sex foster care (2020) and adoption (2022); no rule reaches travelling minors directly.
minors_guardians.interaction: No visitor-specific minor exposure appears; resident family law is tangential.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Under-reported homophobic and transphobic crimes documented (2018, 2024 reports); PDA may draw unwelcome responses outside the capital (travel-guide attribution).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute exists; prosecutors have acted (2018 accommodation-refusal charge); survey shows 63-64% acceptance of LGBT content in schooling.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hate-crime investigations flagged inadequate; victims fear victimisation in trial — recourse is weak but not absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No trans-specific violence figure with denominators; border/document treatment unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Three LGBT centres, multiple Pride events, regional trans march, external equality-body monitoring; a legal-aid structure exists implicitly through community infrastructure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uneven judicial handling limits remedy quality; visitors have community anchors in capital and coastal cities.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor features a universal, visitor-targeted exclusion regime with no remedy. This jurisdiction has no documented visitor-facing exposure at all — no registration, exclusion, raids or targeting — so it is materially safer than any 0.35 anchor.

0.55-B documents actual border secondary screening and entry denial of trans visitors. Here border practice is unresolved, not documented as harmful; only weak recourse signals (under-reporting, inadequate investigations) match that anchor's remedial thinness. This jurisdiction rates above 0.55-B on documented exposures.

0.75-C shows visitor border questioning with functioning remedies. This jurisdiction matches its absence of custodial or criminal threat and its mixed enforcement record, but lacks the documented visitor incidents, placing it slightly above 0.75-C on traveller-facing severity.

0.85-A has documented enforcement gains, oversight findings and quick remedies. This jurisdiction shows the opposite documented pattern — inadequate hate-crime investigation, under-reporting, uneven judiciary — and escalating anti-gender political framing, so it sits below 0.85-A.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of formal acceptance with soft enforcement. No documented rule or practice reaches a trans visitor as exposure: no facility bans, no police campaigns, no visitor arrests, no border documentation of harm — and per rule 1, the absence of stricter machinery is not deducted. Documented structure (hate-crime law covering gender identity, 2013 marker recognition, a codified framework for searching trans persons in police, customs and court settings) is protective in character. The deductions come from recourse quality: hate-crime investigations inadequate, discrimination cases unevenly handled, under-reporting driven by trial victimisation fears, plus tier-3 climate signals — parliamentary anti-gender disinformation and a disrupted Pride. Severity after outing appears limited to friction, weak recourse and occasional hostility, not custody or state targeting. This places the jurisdiction in Reduced Risk, upper band: ~0.72.
